bull.b: Completion of a large, randomized pivotal study with more than 90% power and a defined Q4 2026 readout materially improves development visibility. It gives Inventiva a concrete value inflection point and supports regulatory planning while reducing execution uncertainty.

Statistically significant Phase II composite efficacy, together with FDA Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations, provides clinical validation and regulatory support for lanifibranor. Reported HbA1c, triglyceride, and HDL benefits may also broaden its relevance for MASH patients.

Repayment of EIB loans and restructuring of legacy warrants simplify Inventiva’s capital structure and reduce EIB-linked dilution complexity. Although new warrants still represent potential dilution, the revised arrangement removes restrictive provisions and supports greater financing flexibility.

bear.b: Revenue decline and very large operating losses show that Inventiva has not yet converted development activity into a self-funding commercial model. The 2025 deterioration and persistent cash burn increase reliance on external capital and make progress sensitive to financing access.

Negative shareholder equity across 2023–2025 and substantially higher debt indicate a weakened capital structure. This reduces flexibility to absorb clinical setbacks or fund trials internally, leaving the company more dependent on equity, warrants, or other financing.

Weight gain and fluid retention are known PPAR-gamma class effects that regulators will scrutinize, including possible cardiac safety signals. These tolerability concerns could constrain labeling, prescribing, or commercial uptake even if NATiV3 confirms efficacy.
